 In The High Court At Bombay

Order :

[PER T.V. NALAWADE, J.]
1. The proceeding is filed under section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code for relief of quashing of R.C.C. No.147/2015, presently pending in the Court of J.M.F.C., Parola and which is filed for offences punishable under sections 26(2)(i)(ii)(iii), 3 (1)(zf) and 3 (1) (zz), 31(1), 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standard Act and also under sections 272, 273, 420 of Indian Penal Code.
Both the sides are heard.
2. The crime is registered on the basis of report given by Food Safety Officer on 2.6.2015.

He has made allegations that on that day, his police station received information that at Mangrul, Tahsil Parola, Bhaskar Patil, present applicant was manufacturing milk by using artificial substance for selling the product as milk product and he was attempting to sell it as buffalo milk.
He took action and visited the spot with panchas.
In a room, he noticed that by using mixture, some white material was being created and there were empty polythene bags and also some packs in which milk was filled.
Samples of this milk and also oil which was found there were taken.
In all 540 ltrs. of milk was found there.

As the material found there showed that he was manufacturing the milk for selling and he was using the substance like milk powder, soyadrop oil etc. and he was not having any licence,

1 report was given and the crime was registered for aforesaid offences.
3. There is report of food testing laboratory showing that milk fat noticed was 24.36%.
There was skimmed milk powder detected when it is not permissible to mix the milk powder as per the standards.
Similarly vegetable oil was detected when it is not permissible to mix vegetable oil.
The report shows that the sample did not conform the standards of buffalo milk as laid down in Rule 2.4.1 of aforesaid Special Enactment.
Soyabin oil was also sent to laboratory.
4. The material collected shows that the present applicant was manufacturing milk for selling it as buffalo milk by mixing aforesaid extraneous matters and he had no licence for selling milk.
Thus, he was deceiving the public and he had adulterated the milk.
5. The grounds raised by the learned counsel for applicant are technical grounds.

He submitted that after giving F.I.R., the Food Safety Officer filed private, case which is given number as 163/2015 and due to this circumstance, the F.I.R. and the case on F.I.R. needs to be quashed and set aside.
This proposition is not acceptable.

He placed reliance on some observations made in the cases which are as under :-

11.9.2011 [Suresh Kumar Gupta Vs. State of U.P.]

This point was considered by the Apex Court in Criminal Application No. 1195 of 2018,
(The State of Maharashtra and others Vs. Sayyed Hasan and others) decided on 20.09.2018.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra and others Vs. Sayyed Hasan and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court has considered various provision of aforesaid special enactment and the Apex Court has laid down that when offence punishable under Indian Penal Code is committed and it is cognizable in nature, crime can be registered.

The provision of Section 188 of the Indian Penal Code was considered,
and it is laid down by the Apex Court that when there is prohibitory order and there is breach of the provision, Section 188 of the Indian Penal Code can be used.

The relevant provisions like Section 27 of the General Clauses Act are considered by the Apex Court and it is observed that there is no specific bar for registration of the crime in the scheme of the aforesaid special enactment.
This point was considered by this Court also in Writ Petition No. 3398 of 2011 (Sanket Food Products Private Limited Vs. Union of Indian and others) with connected matters.

entities.text: Sanket Food Products Private Limited Vs. Union of Indian and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that matter also Goa Gutkha was involved and this Court had considered the same challenges raised in the said matter.
In that case manufacturer was also involved.
In the present matter the vendor the person who was in found in possession of prohibited food articles is involved.
Thus, the provision of Section 273 of the Indian Penal Code involving the Food substances which is dangerous to the life can be used in the present matter.
The sample can be tested and ordinarily there is Magnesium Carbonate and there are also heavy metals in such substance.

This Court has considered the provision of the previous Act, The Food Adulteration Act and Rules framed there under and there is not much different in between those provisions and the provisions of new enactment.

It is laid down by this Court that Guthkha is food and if it is sold ( as eatable) and the provisions of the Indian Penal Code like section 272 and 328 of the Indian Penal Code are applicable, the crime can be registered.
In the present matter also this Court hold that these provisions are squarely applicable and so the FIR cannot be quashed.
In the result the application stands dismissed."
7. The scheme of the aforesaid Special Enactment shows that there is no specific bar for registration of crime under IPC.
The act may amount an offence under aforesaid Special Enactment and also under Indian Penal Code.
In view of provision of section 26 of General Clauses Act, the charge can be framed for both the offences, though punishment may not be given under both the provisions for the same act.
In view of these circumstances and as the offence of adulteration and even offence punishable under section 273 of IPC is apparently committed and he was cheating public
, the offence punishable under section 420 of IPC is also committed and so, the police case cannot be quashed.
Both the cases can be clubbed together and can be decided by the Special Judge appointed under the Special Enactment.
So, the case pending before the J.M.F.C. can be sent to Special Judge and by using provision of section 210 of Cr.P.C. both the cases can be clubbed and heard together.
In the result, following order.
O R D E R
The application is dismissed.
R.C.C. No.147/2015 which is pending before J.M.F.C.,
Parola be sent to the Court of Special Judge appointed under aforesaid Special Enactment.
The Special Judge is to decide both the cases together by clubbing together and try as police case.
